chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,
And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except for themselves

He said: He is the one who accuses his wife. So when he accuses her, then he admits that he lied against her, he is whipped the Hadd (penalty), and his wife is returned to him. And if he refuses (to admit lying) and stands by it, so he testifies against her four times with Allah that he is from the truthful ones, and the fifth time then the Curse of Allah be upon him if he is from the liars.

And if she intends to stave off the punishment from herself, and the punishment is the stoning, she testifies four times with Allah that he is from the liars, and the fifth time that the Anger of Allah be upon her if he is from the truthful ones. And if she does not do it, she is stoned; and if she does it, the Hadd is staved off from herself, then she is not permissible for him until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الرَّجْم: Stoning (penalty for married persons committing adultery)
key_terms.تَدْرَأ: To stave off or avert (a penalty)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a husband accuses his wife of adultery without witnesses and she denies it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the specific legal mechanism of *Khul'* (divorce by compensation) triggered by *Hudud al-Zina* (flogging for slander) when a husband accuses his wife of adultery without four witnesses. It details the reciprocal oaths and curses (*Kaffarat al-Yamin*) where the husband’s denial of truthfulness and the wife’s counter-testimony determine whether she avoids stoning, ultimately resulting in a permanent separation (*La tahillu lahu ila yawm al-qiyamah*) even if she accepts the penalty.
